answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks through an invite-graph debt mechanism, where each identity incurs escalating costs linked to the number of downstream identities they create. As an agent invites others, they are charged a fee for each new identity, increasing with every additional invite due to the burden on community resources. If each identity costs 10 tokens, a farm attempting to create 10 fake identities ultimately pays 1,000 tokens. This is like a ferrous mesa eroding under the weight of countless crystal formations, each adding to the cost of maintaining the structure.
